title: The Shor Code
summary: Shor's nine-qubit code concatenates the phase-flip and bit-flip codes and corrects an arbitrary error on one qubit.
objectives: Build the nine-qubit Shor code by encoding the phase-flip code with the bit-flip code
Decode with a majority vote inside each block and then across the block leaders
Explain why correcting X, Y and Z on one qubit also corrects an arbitrary error on that qubit
Tell which two-qubit errors the code corrects and which it turns into a logical error
mission: A real error is rarely a clean X or Z, so the code has to cover every error on one qubit. Complete encode(): a phase-flip code on the block leaders 0, 3 and 6, then a bit-flip code inside each block (0, 1, 2), (3, 4, 5) and (6, 7, 8). Complete decode(): undo the bit-flip codes with a majority vote in each block, then undo the phase-flip code with a majority vote on the leaders. Afterwards qubit 0 must hold the input state again after an X, Y or Z error on any one of the nine qubits, and after an arbitrary rotation on any one qubit, for any input state.

prediction.question: Z errors hit qubits 0 and 1, both in the first block. What happens to the decoded qubit 0?
options: A logical X, as for Z on qubits 0 and 3 in different blocks
A logical Z: two errors in one block beat the inner vote
It is recovered: the two phase flips cancel inside the block
prediction.explanation: A Z on any qubit of a block flips the sign between |000⟩ and |111⟩ in that block. Two of them flip it twice, so the block is back where it started: Z₀Z₁ is a stabilizer, and it acts as the identity on the code. The two-error failures come from other pairs, such as X on 0 and 1 (a logical Z) or Z on 0 and 3 (a logical X).

hints: Encoding has two layers, and the outer one comes first. Which three qubits form the phase-flip code, and what do you apply to them? Then each of those qubits becomes the leader of a bit-flip code on its block.

The outer layer is qml.CNOT(wires=[0, 3]), qml.CNOT(wires=[0, 6]) and a qml.Hadamard on wires 0, 3 and 6. The inner layer is, for each block (a, b, c), qml.CNOT(wires=[a, b]) and qml.CNOT(wires=[a, c]). Decoding runs the same gates in reverse order, with a Toffoli as the vote.

For each block (a, b, c), decode with qml.CNOT(wires=[a, b]), qml.CNOT(wires=[a, c]) and qml.Toffoli(wires=[b, c, a]). Then the leaders 0, 3 and 6 hold a phase-flip code: a Hadamard on each, and the same vote with qml.Toffoli(wires=[3, 6, 0]).
